column1: # The v0.10.0 release notes' ERROR claims: the cells whose answer is a refusal. One per line:
#   <substring the diagnostic must contain>
# Tab-separated, `#` comments ignored. Each program must exit NON-ZERO and its stderr must
# contain the substring. Both halves matter: an exit code without the message is a program
# that failed for some other reason. Each program is ONE line, because that is how the runner
# writes them — Helix has no statement separator, so a claim needing two top-level
# definitions (the duplicate `fn` refusal) is pinned by the corpus program `dup_fn_refused`
# instead of here.
# --- "A negative `take`/`drop` count is an error, on every type ... One sentence everywhere
# --- now" — the String's sentence, which Array used to answer with `[]`.
needs a non-negative count
needs a non-negative count
# --- ADR 0048: "`//` and `%` keep raising on zero", and "A NaN reaching an ordering
# --- comparison still raises with the `is_nan` hint".
zero
zero
is_nan
# --- "The checker knows the range, so `f()` is refused ... in the runtime's words:
# --- `` `f` takes 1 to 2 arguments, got 0 ``".
takes 1 to 2 arguments, got 0
# --- "`s.normalize()` is NFC ... an unknown form is refused by name".
nope
# --- ADR 0052: "The argument list of a frame verb's NAME stays the frame's on any receiver —
# --- a record's `where` receives a predicate through a binding".
a frame's own expression
# --- "PostgreSQL writes: `postgres_execute(url, sql, params?)` ... behind `db-write`" — and
# --- behind `--features postgres`: the verb exists and type-checks everywhere, only the body
# --- is gated (ADR 0032), so a default binary saying so IS the claim.
no PostgreSQL support
